key_insight: GPU-optimized matrix-free solvers accelerate high-order finite element elliptic problems by reducing both iteration counts and per-iteration costs.
engineering_relevance: Faster elliptic solves can reduce computational bottlenecks in large-scale finite element engineering simulations on distributed GPUs.
method: Distributed direct fast diagonalization for tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate.
FD-based hybrid Schwarz and Chebyshev–Jacobi p-multigrid preconditioners supporting hanging-node octrees.
Selective FP32 computation within FP64 conjugate gradients, adaptive coarse-level distribution and multiple-right-hand-side solves.
evidence_signal: Across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPU evaluations, the direct solver was 100–1,000× faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes, while HS-FD converged in 11 iterations on tested octree problems across 8–1,024 MI250X graphics compute dies.
watch_item: Direct fast diagonalization requires compatible tensor-product structure and coefficients; solver choice and FP32 use depend on mesh and coefficient characteristics.
paper_title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
